<STRUCT_0001>
If <MATH_0001> is a Noetherian scheme then any locally closed subset is a
constructible locally closed subset
(Topology, Lemma <REF_0001>).
Hence an abelian sheaf <MATH_0002> on <MATH_0003> is constructible
if and only if there exists a finite partition <MATH_0004>
such that <MATH_0005> is finite locally constant.
(By convention a partition of a topological space has locally
closed parts, see Topology, Section <REF_0002>.)
In other words, we can omit the adjective ``constructible'' in
Definition <REF_0003>. Actually, the category
of constructible sheaves on
Noetherian schemes has some additional properties which we will
catalogue in this section.

Let <MATH_0001> be a Noetherian scheme. Let <MATH_0002> be a Noetherian ring.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> Any sub or quotient sheaf of a constructible sheaf of sets
is constructible.
<STRUCT_0003> The category of constructible abelian sheaves on <MATH_0003> is a
(strong) Serre subcategory of <MATH_0004>. In particular,
every sub and quotient sheaf of a constructible abelian sheaf
on <MATH_0005> is constructible.
<STRUCT_0004> The category of constructible sheaves of <MATH_0006>-modules
on <MATH_0007> is a (strong) Serre subcategory of
<MATH_0008>. In particular, every submodule
and quotient module of a constructible sheaf of <MATH_0009>-modules
on <MATH_0010> is constructible.
<STRUCT_0005>
